Private voice input for Mac

# Hold to talk. Let go, and you get clean text.

Speak naturally and get polished text at your cursor. Speech is recognized on your Mac, and with Ollama, AI tidying happens there too.

Download for Mac
View on GitHub

Free and open source · Your voice is never uploaded · macOS 26+

Notes

You sayUm so I wanted to ask, like, what's the uh rate limit for this API

Pasted at your cursorI wanted to ask what the rate limit for this API is.

Tidy

## How it works

Three steps, in any app.

### Hold the shortcut

Option + Command, in any text field.

### Speak naturally

Pause, correct yourself, think out loud.

### Let go

Clean text appears right at your cursor.

## What you say stays on your Mac

Your voice is always recognized on your Mac. When you want AI tidying, pick a local model and nothing goes online.

### Speech recognition
Always on your Mac
The SenseVoice model runs on your Mac. Recordings are never uploaded.

### AI tidying
Your choice
With Ollama, LM Studio, or Apple Intelligence, your text stays on your Mac too. With a cloud service, only the recognized text is sent.

### Everything else
Nothing collected
No account and no tracking in the app. Recent results live in memory and are cleared when you quit.

See what leaves your Mac in each setup →

## Keep AI tidying on your Mac too

Run a local model with Ollama or LM Studio and Tidytalk never needs the internet to clean up your words.

- Choose Ollama, LM Studio, Cloud, or Apple Intelligence in one click
- No API key, and nothing sent over the internet
- Prefer the cloud? DeepSeek, OpenAI, or any compatible API works too

## It learns the words you use

Names, products, and jargon are what speech recognition gets wrong. Teach Tidytalk once.

- Common words fix similar-sounding mistakes
- Replacements always correct the same slip
- Snippets turn a short phrase into your email or address

## Live captions for what your Mac plays

Press ⌃⌥C to caption a video, a lecture, or a meeting. The audio is recognized on your Mac, just like your voice.

- Listen to all audio, or just one app
- Translate as you listen, shown under the original
- Press ⌃⌥V to paste what was just said
- Transcribe audio, video files, and links too

## Turn recordings and videos into text

Drop in a meeting recording, a lecture, or a video, or paste a YouTube or Bilibili link. Tidytalk transcribes it on your Mac.

- A timestamp for every sentence
- Export as text, SRT subtitles, or Markdown
- For links, only the audio is downloaded, then deleted

How to transcribe meetings and videos →

## Pick the speech model that fits

SenseVoice is small and fast. When you need more accuracy or more languages, switch models in one click. Every model runs on your Mac.

- Qwen3-ASR recognizes names and terms from your vocabulary
- Whisper Turbo covers about 99 languages
- Or use the speech recognition built into macOS

## Why Tidytalk

Small, private, and yours to change.

### Works offline

With a local model, Tidytalk works without an internet connection.

### Free and open source

MIT licensed. No account and no word limits.

### Tidies, never invents

Removes fillers and slips without summarizing or adding.

### Speak one language, write another

Translate into 8 languages as you dictate.

### Rewrite with your voice

Select text, hold Right Option, and say what to change.

### Leaves your clipboard alone

Whatever you copied is restored after pasting.

## Made for the way you work

### For developers

Prompts, commit messages, and code comments.

### Dictate and translate

Speak Chinese, paste English.

### Private and offline

Keep your voice and your text on your Mac.

### Transcribe recordings

Meetings, lectures, and videos to text.

Comparing options? See Tidytalk vs Wispr Flow, Superwhisper, and macOS Dictation.

## Questions

**Is Tidytalk free?**

Yes. Tidytalk is free and open source under the MIT License. If you tidy text with a cloud AI service such as DeepSeek or OpenAI, you use your own API key and the provider bills you. With a local model in Ollama or LM Studio, or with tidying off, it costs nothing.

**Does it need an internet connection?**

Speech recognition needs it only once, to download the speech model (about 240 MB) on first launch. Tidying with a cloud AI service needs a connection; with a local model or with tidying off, the whole app works offline.

**Which languages does it support?**

With the default SenseVoice model it detects the spoken language automatically and supports Mandarin Chinese (including mixed-in English), English, Japanese, Korean, and Cantonese. For other languages, switch to Qwen3-ASR (30 languages and 22 Chinese dialects) or Whisper Turbo (about 99) in Settings › Speech Model. Text can also be translated into English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, or Spanish. The interface is available in English and Simplified Chinese.

**Is my voice or text uploaded?**

Your voice never is. Recording and speech recognition happen on your Mac. With Tidy up text on, the recognized text is sent to the AI service you set up; with a local model or with tidying off, text never leaves your Mac either.

**Can it caption videos and meetings?**

Yes. Press ⌃⌥C (Control + Option + C) and Tidytalk shows live captions for whatever your Mac is playing, such as a video, a lecture, or a meeting. The audio is recognized on your Mac. You can translate each sentence with your AI service, and press ⌃⌥V to tidy and paste what was just said.

**Is there a free, open-source alternative to Wispr Flow for Mac?**

Yes, Tidytalk. Like Wispr Flow, you hold a shortcut, speak, and get clean, punctuated text at your cursor in any app. Unlike Wispr Flow, speech is recognized on your Mac, there's no account, subscription, or weekly word limit, and the code is open source under the MIT License. See how the two compare.

**How do I transcribe a meeting recording on Mac without uploading it?**

Choose Transcribe File or Link from the Tidytalk menu and drop in the audio or video file, up to 3 hours long. It's recognized on your Mac and split into paragraphs with timestamps, and you can export it as TXT, SRT, or Markdown. YouTube and Bilibili links work too. Learn more about transcribing.

**How is it different from macOS Dictation?**

Dictation types your words as you speak. Tidytalk waits until you finish a whole paragraph, removes fillers and slips, adds punctuation, and then inserts the result in one go, which suits messages, email, and documents.

**Does it run on Windows or Intel Macs?**

No. Tidytalk requires macOS 26 or later on a Mac with Apple silicon.

**macOS says it can't verify the developer. What should I do?**

The app isn't notarized by Apple yet. Open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click "Open Anyway" at the bottom. Or run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Tidytalk.app in Terminal, and it will open normally from then on.

## Stop typing what you can say.

Download for Mac
Read the user guide

Free · No account required · macOS 26+

# Tidytalk user guide

Everything Tidytalk can do, from your first dictation to local AI models and troubleshooting.

{{updated}}

## Install and set up

Tidytalk needs macOS 26 or later on a Mac with Apple silicon.

- Download the latest Tidytalk-x.y.z.dmg from GitHub Releases, open it, and drag Tidytalk into the Applications folder.

- The app isn't notarized by Apple yet, so macOS blocks it the first time. Open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click "Open Anyway" at the bottom, or run this in Terminal:
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Tidytalk.app

- Follow the setup guide that opens:

- Allow Microphone so Tidytalk can record.

- Allow Accessibility so it can detect the shortcut and paste text at your cursor.

- Set Up AI: enter an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, API key, and model. DeepSeek is the default. You can skip this and get the raw transcript instead.

- Download Speech Model: about 240 MB, once. After that, recognition works offline.

Tidytalk lives in the menu bar. It only appears in the Dock while its setup guide or main window is open. Open the menu bar icon for settings, recent results, and the output language; settings are also at the bottom left of the main window, or press ⌘,.

## Hold to talk

- Put your cursor in any text field.

- Hold Option + Command and speak. A glass indicator appears at the bottom of the screen and moves with your voice.

- Let go. After a moment, the tidied text appears at your cursor.

- Recording starts after you hold the keys for about 0.4 seconds, so ordinary shortcuts such as Option + Command + a letter don't trigger it.

- Press another key, click the mouse, or press Esc while holding to cancel.

- One recording can be up to about 2 minutes. Recordings shorter than half a second are ignored.

- Change the shortcut in Settings › Dictation. You can choose Control, Option, Command, Fn (🌐), Right Option, or Right Command. If you choose Fn, set "Press 🌐 key to" to "Do Nothing" in System Settings › Keyboard, or macOS opens emoji or Dictation at the same time.

- Live text appears under the indicator while you speak. It's only a preview: the final result is recognized and tidied after you let go.

- If there's nowhere to type, for example the focus is on the desktop or a web page, the result is copied to the clipboard instead of pasted.

- Your clipboard is restored after pasting, including images, files, and rich text.

## Hands-free recording

Double-tap the shortcut to start recording without holding the keys, which is handy for longer thoughts. Press the shortcut once more to finish, or Esc to cancel. Typing and clicking don't interrupt a hands-free recording. When you talk for a long time, Tidytalk recognizes what you've already said while you keep talking, so the text is ready soon after you finish. You can turn this off in Settings › Dictation.

## Rewrite selected text

Select some text, hold Right Option, and say how to change it, such as "make it more formal", "shorten this to one sentence", or "translate to English". When you let go, the selection is replaced with the rewrite.

- This needs an AI service. The selected text and your instruction are sent to it.

- If nothing is selected, Tidytalk asks you to select text first. If the rewrite fails, your text isn't changed.

- Change or turn off the rewrite shortcut in Settings › Dictation.

## Control from other apps

Tidytalk responds to tidytalk:// links, so you can start dictation from Raycast, Shortcuts, Karabiner, or a Stream Deck:

Link | What it does

tidytalk://toggle | Start dictation, like double-tapping the shortcut; open it again to finish

tidytalk://start / tidytalk://stop | Only start, or only finish

tidytalk://cancel | Cancel the current recording

tidytalk://captions | Turn live captions on or off; also captions/start and captions/stop

In Terminal or a script, use open -g tidytalk://toggle so focus stays where you're typing. If opening a link brings Tidytalk to the front, it hands focus back to the app you were in, so the text still lands at your cursor.

## Speech models

SenseVoice is the default: small (about 240 MB), fast, and great with mixed Chinese and English. In Settings › Speech Model you can switch to another model. All of them run on your Mac.

- Qwen3-ASR (about 1 GB): the most accurate, with 30 languages and 22 Chinese dialects, and it recognizes names and terms from your vocabulary. About 4 seconds for 20 seconds of speech.

- Fun-ASR-Nano (about 1 GB): Chinese, English, and Japanese, nearly as accurate as Qwen3-ASR and a bit faster.

- Whisper Turbo (about 1 GB): about 99 languages, good for less common ones. It drops characters in Chinese.

- Apple Speech: built into macOS, nothing to download. It recognizes your system language and is weaker on mixed Chinese and English.

Click the download button and keep working: the current model is used until the download finishes. Dictation, live captions, and file transcription all use the model you choose.

## Live captions

Tidytalk can caption whatever your Mac is playing, such as a video, a lecture, or a video call. It records only the computer's audio, never the microphone, and recognizes it on your Mac.

- Turn it on or off: press ⌃⌥C (Control + Option + C), or choose Start Listening under Live Captions in the menu bar menu. The first time, macOS asks to allow Tidytalk to record system audio. While listening, the menu bar icon shows an orange dot. Turning captions off clears the audio and text from memory.

- The caption bar: one sentence per line, with earlier sentences dimmed. Drag it anywhere and it remembers the spot. It hides after 10 seconds of silence and comes back when there's sound. Hover over it for translate, pause, and close buttons; close stops listening. Clicking a sentence does nothing, so you can drag freely. Choose a dark or glass style and a text size in Settings › Live Captions.

- What it listens to: all audio except Tidytalk's own sounds, or a single app you pick under Listen To in the menu or in Settings › Live Captions.

- Translation: turn on Translate Captions and sentences are translated with your Set Up AI service and shown under the original. Sentences already in the target language are left alone. With "Translate as You Listen" on (the default), the sentence being spoken is translated too and updates as it goes, then the final translation replaces it; turn it off to translate only finished sentences and make fewer AI calls. With Ollama, LM Studio, or Apple Intelligence, nothing goes online; with a cloud service, caption text is sent to it.

- Paste what was just said: while listening, put your cursor in a text field and press ⌃⌥V. Tidytalk tidies the latest passage (since the last pause of more than 2 seconds, up to 30 seconds) with your dictation settings and pastes it. You can also hover over a sentence in the captions and click Paste to paste from there onward. ⌃⌥V only works while captions are on; the rest of the time other apps can use it.

For a step-by-step walkthrough, see Live translated captions for videos and meetings.

## Meeting recording

Press ⌃⌥M (Control + Option + M), or start from the menu bar or the Meetings page of the Tidytalk window. Tidytalk records your microphone and your Mac's audio (the people on the other end) at the same time. Press it again to stop.

- During the meeting: each sentence appears as a draft as soon as it's spoken, with "Me" and "Others" in two colors. Dictation keeps working. Meeting recording and live captions can't run at the same time.

- After the meeting: Tidytalk tells speakers apart and transcribes again on your Mac (about 5 minutes for an hour). The other side is split into Speaker 1, 2, 3, which you can rename. Moments when several people talk at once are marked, and that text is transcribed from the mixed audio. If the split looks wrong, set how many people were on the other side and run it again.

- Without headphones: your microphone also picks up the other side from your speakers. Tidytalk turns on the system's echo cancellation and removes your lines that match theirs at the same moment.

- AI summary: key points, decisions, to-dos, and open questions. With Ollama, LM Studio, or Apple Intelligence the text stays on your Mac; with a cloud service the meeting text is sent to that service.

- Where it's stored: text and recordings stay on your Mac (~/Library/Application Support/Tidytalk/Meetings), about 30 MB per hour. Delete a meeting, or just its recording, at any time.

- Telling speakers apart needs a one-time download of about 29 MB. Without it, Tidytalk only separates "Me" and "Others". Needs microphone and system audio recording permission.

## Transcribe files and links

Choose "Transcribe File or Link…" in the menu bar menu, or open Transcribe in the Tidytalk window. The page has two tabs, Files and Links:

- Files: drop an audio or video file (MP3, M4A, WAV, MP4, MOV and more, up to 3 hours) onto the page, or click the drop area to choose one. Tidytalk remembers where the file is and doesn't copy it.

- Links: paste a video link (YouTube, Bilibili, and more). The first time, Tidytalk downloads the open-source tool yt-dlp (about 35 MB) from its official GitHub release, checks it against the checksum published there, and updates it every two weeks. Only the audio and cover image are downloaded. They stay on your Mac and can be deleted anytime. Use only content you have the right to use.

- Every transcription is saved as a card. Open it to play the audio, fix a line, copy everything, or export plain text (.txt), subtitles (.srt), or Markdown. Downloaded audio can be saved elsewhere, or deleted while keeping the text.

- It uses the speech model from Settings › Speech Model and runs on your Mac.

## How tidying works

Tidying only removes and corrects. It doesn't change what you said:

- Filler words such as "um", "uh", and "like" (and 嗯、那个、就是说 in Chinese) are removed.

- Repeated words and slips are removed. When you correct yourself, only the corrected version is kept.

- Punctuation is added, and long speech is split into sentences.

- It never summarizes or adds content. English words and technical terms inside Chinese speech are kept as they are.

- Text that sounds like a command, such as "write me an email", is tidied into text, not carried out.

You say | You get

Um so I wanted to ask, like, what's the uh rate limit for this API | I wanted to ask what the rate limit for this API is.

Let's move the launch to Wednesday, no wait, Thursday | Let's move the launch to Thursday.

Turn off "Tidy up text" in Settings › Set Up AI to paste the raw transcript. Tidytalk then works fully offline. If the AI service is slow, unreachable, or returns something unexpected, Tidytalk pastes the raw transcript and tells you.

## Cleanup strength and mode

Both are in Settings › Set Up AI › Tidying.

Strength | What it does

Light | Only adds punctuation and removes fillers like "um" and "uh". Everything else stays as you said it.

Standard (default) | Removes fillers and slips, and adds punctuation.

Thorough | Also tightens wordy or repetitive phrasing, without changing the meaning.

Mode | What it does

Standard (default) | Removes fillers, fixes slips, and adds punctuation, keeping your meaning.

Chat (casual) | Keeps a casual tone and sentence-final particles. Good for messages.

Email (formal) | Uses formal, complete sentences. Good for email and documents.

Code (keep terms) | Keeps terms, commands, file names, and symbols exactly as they are and leaves punctuation alone. Good for technical writing.

## Output language

By default the output is in the language you spoke. Choose another output language and the text is translated as it's tidied, so you can speak Chinese and paste an English email. Tidytalk can translate into English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, and Spanish.

- Change it in Settings › Set Up AI › Tidying, or quickly from the "Output Language" submenu in the menu bar.

- Translation and tidying happen in one request, so it's about as fast as tidying alone. Your vocabulary and mode still apply.

- Translation needs "Tidy up text" turned on. If the request fails, the original text is pasted.

See Dictate and translate for examples.

## Local AI models

Tidytalk talks to AI services with the OpenAI-compatible protocol, so it also works with models running on your Mac. Then your text never leaves the computer.

- Install Ollama and download a model, for example ollama pull qwen2.5:7b. Or download and load a model in LM Studio and start its local server.

- At the top of Settings › Set Up AI, choose Ollama or LM Studio, confirm the model name, and save. To go back to DeepSeek, OpenAI, or another online service, choose Cloud. Local models don't need an API key, and the timeout is raised to 60 seconds.

- Click the purple network icon to test the connection.

Reasoning models such as Qwen3 or DeepSeek-R1 work too: Tidytalk asks the service to skip thinking and removes any thinking that still comes back. Results depend on the model size. Small models follow "tidy, don't answer" and custom rules less reliably than cloud models, so a model around 7B or larger is recommended. See Private and offline dictation for details.

### Apple Intelligence

On a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence, choose Apple Intelligence in Settings › Set Up AI to tidy and translate with the model built into macOS. No API key is needed, and your text never leaves your Mac. Turn on Apple Intelligence in System Settings first; if this Mac doesn't support it or it's off, the option is dimmed and says why.

## Vocabulary

All of these are in Settings › Vocabulary.

### Common words

List names, products, and terms you use, one per line. These are the words speech recognition gets wrong most often. With Qwen3-ASR as the speech model, they're recognized correctly from the start. They're also added to the AI prompt so similar-sounding mistakes are corrected to your spelling, which requires "Tidy up text". Even with tidying off, close matches are fixed on your Mac: different capitalization or spacing ("github" → "GitHub", "chat gpt" → "ChatGPT"), a letter off in a long word ("Kubernetis" → "Kubernetes"), and Chinese words of three or more characters that sound the same ("张三峰" → "张三丰"). Words inside links, email addresses, and file paths aren't touched.

### Replacements

Always replace one spelling with another, for example "cloud" with "Claude". English matching ignores case and only matches whole words. Replacements run on your Mac, even with tidying off. From "Recent" in the menu bar, choose a result and "Add to Vocabulary…" to add a misheard word directly.

### Words you correct

If you change a word in the same text field after pasting, such as "cloud" to "Claude", Tidytalk lists it under "Edits Found" in the menu bar and at the top of Settings › Vocabulary. Nothing is added until you click "Add to Vocabulary". It only compares within about a minute and a half of pasting and saves nothing. Turn it off at the bottom of the Vocabulary page.

### Snippets

Say only a phrase such as "my email" to insert a full email address or a canned reply. The snippet is used only when the whole recording is that phrase, never when it appears inside a sentence.

### Custom rules

Write your own rules, one per line, such as "Write amounts as digits" or "Write the product name as Tidytalk". Tidying and voice rewrite follow them. Rules only affect how things are written; they never make the AI add content. Up to 20 rules.

Not sure which to use? See how to make dictation get names and terms right.

## Chinese–English spacing

Tidytalk adds spaces between Chinese and English or numbers, uses full-width punctuation after Chinese, and converts full-width letters and digits to half-width. Decimal points, file names, and URLs aren't affected. This runs on your Mac and can be turned off in Settings › General.

## Recent results

Your last 20 results are kept in memory. From "Recent" in the menu bar you can paste or copy one again, copy the raw transcript, re-tidy it with another mode or language and paste it into the current text field, or add a misheard word to your vocabulary. Nothing is written to disk, and the list is cleared when you quit.

## Supported languages

You don't choose a language before speaking. Tidytalk detects it automatically. With the default SenseVoice model, it supports:

- Mandarin Chinese, including English words and technical terms mixed in

- English

- Japanese

- Korean

- Cantonese (written in Simplified Chinese, keeping Cantonese wording)

For other spoken languages, switch the speech model in Settings › Speech Model: Qwen3-ASR covers 30 languages and 22 Chinese dialects, such as Sichuanese, Northeastern, Wu, and Minnan, and Whisper Turbo covers about 99 languages. You can also speak one language and set the output language to write in another. The interface is available in English and Simplified Chinese and follows your system language.

Mixing Chinese and English? See how to dictate mixed Chinese and English.

## Troubleshooting

What happens | Why, and what to do

"Cleanup failed, pasted original" | The AI service was unreachable, timed out, or returned something unusual. Check your network and click the purple network icon in Settings › Set Up AI to test the connection.

"Didn't hear anything" | Nothing was recognized. Check the microphone in Settings › Dictation.

The shortcut does nothing | Accessibility access is missing. Allow it in Settings › General › Permissions.

macOS says it can't verify the developer | The app isn't notarized yet. Click "Open Anyway" in System Settings › Privacy & Security.

### Accessibility still shows as not allowed

If Tidytalk is turned on in System Settings but still shows as not allowed, the list probably has an entry from an older version. In System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility, select Tidytalk, click "−" to remove it, then click "Allow" in Tidytalk to add it again. Or run:
tccutil reset Accessibility app.tidytalk.Tidytalk

All settings are stored in ~/.tidytalk.json, which you can edit directly. Your API key is kept in the macOS Keychain instead of that file. See the configuration reference.

## Uninstall

Dragging Tidytalk to the Trash removes only the app. The speech model, settings, and permission records stay on your Mac. To remove everything, quit Tidytalk (turn off "Open at login" first if you enabled it), move the app to the Trash, and run:
rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/Tidytalk
rm -f ~/.tidytalk.json
security delete-generic-password -s app.tidytalk.Tidytalk -a ai.api_key
rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/app.tidytalk.Tidytalk ~/Library/HTTPStorages/app.tidytalk.Tidytalk
defaults delete app.tidytalk.Tidytalk
tccutil reset All app.tidytalk.Tidytalk

These remove the speech models (SenseVoice is about 240 MB, other models about 1 GB each), the speaker model, yt-dlp, your meetings, your settings, your API key in the Keychain, network caches, preferences, and microphone, accessibility, and system audio recording permissions. Keep ~/.tidytalk.json if you plan to reinstall and want your settings back.

# Tidytalk vs Wispr Flow vs Superwhisper vs macOS Dictation

Four ways to talk instead of type on a Mac. Here's how they differ on price, privacy, and what happens to your words.

{{updated}}

Tidytalk is our project, so we've kept this page factual. Competitor details come from their official websites and help pages, checked in October 2026. Prices and features change, so check each product's site before you decide.

## At a glance

| Tidytalk | Wispr Flow | Superwhisper | macOS Dictation

Price | Free | Free up to 2,000 words a week on desktop; Pro $15/month, or $12/month billed yearly | Free plan with local models; Pro $8.49/month, $84.99/year, or $249.99 once | Free, built in

Platforms | Mac (macOS 26+, Apple silicon) | Mac, Windows, iOS, Android | Mac, Windows, iOS, Android | Mac and other Apple devices

Where your voice is recognized | On your Mac | In the cloud | On your Mac with local models, or in the cloud | On your Mac for supported languages on Apple silicon; otherwise Apple's servers

Removes fillers and fixes slips | Yes, with an AI service you choose | Yes | Yes, with AI modes on Pro | No, types what you say

Works fully offline | Yes, with a local model or tidying off | No | Yes, with local models | Yes, for supported languages

Open source | Yes, MIT | No | No | No

## Tidytalk

Tidytalk is paragraph-style: you hold a shortcut, say a whole thought, and let go. Speech is recognized on your Mac with the SenseVoice model, then an AI service you pick removes fillers and slips and adds punctuation before the text is pasted at your cursor.

- You control where text goes. Use DeepSeek, OpenAI, or any OpenAI-compatible service with your own API key, or a local model in Ollama or LM Studio so nothing leaves your Mac. Your voice is never uploaded.

- Free and open source. No word limits or subscriptions. With a cloud AI service, you pay the provider directly for what you use.

- Strong for mixed Chinese and English. It handles English terms inside Chinese speech, adds Chinese–English spacing, and can translate as it tidies.

- Limits to know about: Mac only, and only macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon. It recognizes five spoken languages: Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, and Cantonese. The app isn't notarized yet, so you approve it once in System Settings. Using AI cleanup means setting up an API key or a local model.

## Wispr Flow

Wispr Flow is a polished commercial app that turns speech into clean writing in any app, and it learns your names and jargon. It runs on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, which makes it the easiest choice if you dictate across devices.

- The free plan allows 2,000 words a week on desktop and 1,000 on mobile. Pro removes the limit for $15 a month, or $12 a month billed yearly.

- According to Wispr's own help center, transcription always runs in the cloud. Privacy settings control model training and storage, not where audio is processed, so there's no offline mode.

Looking for something like Wispr Flow that's free and runs on your Mac? See Tidytalk as a Wispr Flow alternative.

## Superwhisper

Superwhisper is a feature-rich commercial app with configurable AI modes that reformat what you say, from casual messages to structured notes. It runs on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android.

- It can transcribe offline with local models, which its FAQ says run best on Apple silicon Macs. Cloud models are also available.

- The free plan includes unlimited dictation with local Whisper models. AI modes, cloud models, and file transcription need Pro: $8.49 a month, $84.99 a year, or $249.99 once. Pro's local AI model works in English only.

See Tidytalk as a Superwhisper alternative for a closer comparison.

## macOS Dictation

Dictation is built into macOS, free, and needs no setup. On Apple silicon Macs, supported languages are processed on the device. It types your words as you speak, so it's great for quick input, but it keeps fillers and doesn't clean up or restructure what you said. It stops automatically after 30 seconds of silence.

## Which one should you choose?

- Choose Tidytalk if you want a free, open-source tool, care where your text is sent, or dictate in Chinese mixed with English.

- Choose Wispr Flow if you want the same dictation on Windows and your phone and don't mind cloud processing or a subscription.

- Choose Superwhisper if you want lots of customizable AI modes and offline models on several platforms, and are happy to pay for Pro.

- Stick with macOS Dictation if you only need quick, word-for-word input and don't need fillers removed.

Considering Typeless? See Tidytalk as a Typeless alternative.

## Sources

- Wispr Flow pricing and Understanding Privacy Mode and Cloud Sync

- Superwhisper plans and pricing and language models

- Apple: Dictate messages and documents on Mac

# A free, open-source Wispr Flow alternative for Mac

Like Wispr Flow, Tidytalk turns what you say into clean, punctuated text at your cursor in any app. Unlike Wispr Flow, your voice is recognized on your Mac, there's no subscription, and the code is open source.

{{updated}}

Tidytalk is our project, so we've kept this page factual. Wispr Flow details come from its official pricing and help pages, checked in October 2026. Products change, so check their sites before you decide.

## What works the same

- Hold a shortcut, speak naturally, and let go. The text appears wherever your cursor is: email, chat, notes, a code editor.

- Filler words and slips are removed and punctuation is added, so you don't have to edit afterward.

- You can teach it names, products, and jargon it keeps getting wrong.

- You can speak one language and get text in another.

## What's different

| Tidytalk | Wispr Flow

Price | Free, no word limits | Free up to 2,000 words a week on desktop; Pro $15/month, or $12/month billed yearly

Where your voice is recognized | On your Mac (SenseVoice, Qwen3-ASR, Whisper, or Apple's built-in recognition) | In the cloud

AI cleanup | Your choice: Ollama, LM Studio, or Apple Intelligence on your Mac, or a cloud API with your own key | Built in, in the cloud

Works fully offline | Yes, with a local model or with cleanup off | No

Account | None | Required

Platforms | Mac (macOS 26+, Apple silicon) | Mac, Windows, iOS, Android

Open source | Yes, MIT License | No

Tidytalk also does a few things beyond dictation: live captions for audio your Mac is playing, with translation as you listen, and transcription of audio and video files or YouTube and Bilibili links.

## When Wispr Flow is the better choice

- You want the same dictation on Windows or your phone.

- You'd rather not set anything up: no model download, no AI service to choose.

- You use an Intel Mac or a macOS version older than 26.

## When Tidytalk is the better choice

- You don't want your voice to leave your Mac, or you need dictation that works offline.

- You dictate a lot and don't want a weekly word limit or a subscription.

- You speak Chinese mixed with English: Tidytalk keeps the English terms and adds Chinese–English spacing.

- You want to read the code or change it yourself.

## Switching from Wispr Flow

- Download Tidytalk, drag it into Applications, and follow the setup guide to allow the microphone and accessibility and download the speech model.

- Pick your shortcut in Settings › Dictation. If you're used to holding Fn, choose Fn (🌐), then set "Press 🌐 key to" to "Do Nothing" in System Settings › Keyboard.

- Add the names and terms from your Wispr Flow dictionary to Settings › Vocabulary. With Qwen3-ASR as the speech model, they're recognized correctly from the start.

- Choose an AI service in Settings › Set Up AI: Ollama or LM Studio to keep everything on your Mac, Apple Intelligence if your Mac supports it, or a cloud API such as DeepSeek or OpenAI.

## Sources

- Wispr Flow pricing and Understanding Privacy Mode and Cloud Sync

- For Superwhisper and macOS Dictation too, see the full comparison.

# A free, open-source Superwhisper alternative for Mac

Superwhisper and Tidytalk both turn speech into text at your cursor and can run fully on your Mac. The difference: in Tidytalk, AI cleanup is free, works with any local or cloud model in any language, and the code is open source.

{{updated}}

Tidytalk is our project, so we've kept this page factual. Superwhisper details come from its official documentation, checked in October 2026. Products change, so check their site before you decide.

## At a glance

| Tidytalk | Superwhisper

Price | Free, everything included | Free plan; Pro $8.49/month, $84.99/year, or $249.99 once

Speech recognition | On your Mac: SenseVoice, Qwen3-ASR, Fun-ASR-Nano, Whisper Turbo, or Apple's built-in recognition | Local Whisper models on Free; more local models and cloud models on Pro

AI cleanup | Free, with Ollama, LM Studio, Apple Intelligence, or any OpenAI-compatible API | Pro only. Cloud models, or a small local model that's English only

Fully offline with AI cleanup | Yes, in any language your local model handles | Yes, in English, with the local S1-mini model

Platforms | Mac (macOS 26+, Apple silicon) | Mac, Windows, iOS, Android

Open source | Yes, MIT License | No

Both have custom vocabulary and text replacements. Tidytalk also includes live captions with translation for any audio your Mac plays, and transcription of files and YouTube or Bilibili links, all free.

## When Superwhisper is the better choice

- You want the same app on Windows, iPhone, or Android.

- You want many customizable AI modes, a meeting assistant, or team features like SSO.

- You use an Intel Mac or a macOS version older than 26.

## When Tidytalk is the better choice

- You want AI cleanup without paying for a subscription or a license.

- You want cleanup to stay on your Mac in Chinese, Japanese, or another language, not just English.

- You speak Chinese mixed with English. Tidytalk's default model is built for it and adds Chinese–English spacing.

- You want to read the code or change it yourself.

## Switching from Superwhisper

- Download Tidytalk and follow the setup guide.

- Copy your custom vocabulary into Settings › Vocabulary › Common Words, and your text replacements into Replacements.

- Instead of modes, pick a cleanup mode (Standard, Chat, Email, or Code) in Settings › Set Up AI › Tidying, and add your own instructions as Custom Rules.

- To keep everything local, choose Ollama, LM Studio, or Apple Intelligence as the AI service. See private and offline dictation.

# A free, offline Typeless alternative for Mac

Typeless and Tidytalk both turn natural speech into polished text, removing fillers and fixing self-corrections. Typeless does it in the cloud with an account and a subscription. Tidytalk does it on your Mac, for free, with no account.

{{updated}}

Tidytalk is our project, so we've kept this page factual. Typeless details come from its official pricing and data controls pages, checked in October 2026. Products change, so check their site before you decide.

## At a glance

| Tidytalk | Typeless

Price | Free, no word limits | Free plan with a weekly word limit; Pro $12/month billed yearly, or $30/month billed monthly

Where your voice is recognized | On your Mac | In the cloud

AI cleanup | Your choice: Ollama, LM Studio, or Apple Intelligence on your Mac, or a cloud API with your own key | Built in, in the cloud

Works offline | Yes, with a local model or with cleanup off | No

Account | None | Required

Platforms | Mac (macOS 26+, Apple silicon) | Mac, Windows, iOS, Android, and Linux

Open source | Yes, MIT License | No

Typeless says audio isn't stored and its AI providers don't keep or train on your data. With Tidytalk, audio never leaves your Mac in the first place.

## What works the same

- Speak naturally in any app and get clean text: fillers and repetitions removed, self-corrections resolved, punctuation added.

- A personal dictionary for names and terms.

- Speak one language and get text in another.

- Edit text by voice: select it and say what to change.

## When Typeless is the better choice

- You want the same dictation on Windows, Linux, or your phone.

- You'd rather not set anything up: no model download and no AI service to choose.

- You use an Intel Mac or a macOS version older than 26.

## When Tidytalk is the better choice

- You don't want your voice to leave your Mac, or you need dictation that works offline.

- You dictate a lot and don't want a weekly word limit, a subscription, or an account.

- You speak Chinese mixed with English. Tidytalk keeps the English terms and adds Chinese–English spacing.

- You also want live captions for videos and meetings, or transcription of recordings, at no cost.

## Switching from Typeless

- Download Tidytalk and follow the setup guide.

- Copy the words from your Typeless dictionary into Settings › Vocabulary › Common Words.

- Choose an AI service in Settings › Set Up AI. Ollama, LM Studio, or Apple Intelligence keep everything on your Mac.

- Pick a shortcut in Settings › Dictation. Voice editing of selected text uses Right Option by default.

# Turn recordings and videos into text, on your Mac

Meeting recordings, lectures, interviews, and videos become timestamped text you can copy or export. The audio is recognized on your Mac and never uploaded.

{{updated}}

## How to transcribe a file

- Click the Tidytalk icon in the menu bar and choose "Transcribe File or Link…". This opens the Transcribe page in the Tidytalk window. Use the Files tab.

- Drop an audio or video file onto the page, or click the drop area to choose one. MP3, M4A, WAV, MP4, MOV and other common formats work, up to 3 hours long.

- Tidytalk splits the recording at pauses and recognizes it sentence by sentence. Each sentence shows when it was said.

- Each transcription is kept as a card. Open it to play it back or fix a line, and use the copy and export buttons at the top to get the text as plain text, SRT subtitles, or Markdown.

## Transcribe a video link

On the Links tab, paste a link to a single video from YouTube, Bilibili, or another site, and press Return or click the arrow button. The first time, Tidytalk downloads yt-dlp, an open-source download tool (about 35 MB), from its official GitHub release and checks it against the published checksum. After that, only the video's audio and cover image are downloaded. They stay on your Mac: the card shows the cover and length, and you can play or save the audio, or delete it and keep the text.

Use links only for content you have the right to use. Videos that need you to sign in, playlists, and live streams aren't supported.

## Which speech model to use

File transcription uses the model you choose in Settings › Speech Model. All of them run on your Mac.

Model | Best for

SenseVoice (default) | Fast transcripts in Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, or Cantonese, including mixed Chinese and English.

Qwen3-ASR | The most accurate results and the best punctuation, in 30 languages and 22 Chinese dialects. It also recognizes names and terms from your vocabulary.

Whisper Turbo | Less common languages; it covers about 99. Use another model for Chinese.

## Export formats

- Plain text (.txt): paragraphs split at longer pauses, ready for notes or an AI summary.

- Subtitles (.srt): one cue per sentence with start and end times, for video editors and players.

- Markdown (.md): the title and each sentence with its timestamp, for docs and wikis.

## Tips and limits

- Clear audio with one person speaking at a time gives the best results. Background music and people talking over each other lower accuracy.

- Tidytalk doesn't label who is speaking.

- Your replacements and Chinese–English spacing are applied to the transcript, just like dictation.

- For a meeting that's happening right now, use live captions instead: press ⌃⌥C to caption what your Mac is playing as it plays.

## Privacy

Recognition happens on your Mac, so recordings are never uploaded. Transcripts stay in the window until you copy or export them, and nothing is saved anywhere else. For links, the only network traffic is downloading yt-dlp once and the video's audio.

---

URL: https://tidytalk.zayen.dev/use-cases/offline/

# Dictation that never leaves your Mac

Tidytalk always recognizes your voice on your Mac. Pair it with a local model and your text stays there too.

{{updated}}

## What leaves your Mac

Setup | Your voice | Your text

Cloud AI service (for example DeepSeek or OpenAI) | Stays on your Mac | Sent to the AI service you chose

Local model in Ollama or LM Studio | Stays on your Mac | Stays on your Mac

"Tidy up text" turned off | Stays on your Mac | Stays on your Mac (raw transcript)

Speech recognition uses the SenseVoice model, which runs on your Mac after a one-time download of about 240 MB. Recent results are kept in memory only and cleared when you quit. Settings are stored in ~/.tidytalk.json, readable only by you, and your API key is kept in the macOS Keychain.

Apart from the AI service you set up, Tidytalk only goes online to download models, check for updates (at launch, at most once a day, which you can turn off in Settings › General), and transcribe links. Each case is listed in the privacy policy.

## Set up Ollama

- Install Ollama.

- Download a model in Terminal, for example:
ollama pull qwen2.5:7b

- In Tidytalk, open Settings › Set Up AI, and choose Ollama at the top. Check that the model name matches the one you pulled, then click the checkmark button to save.

- Click the purple network icon next to it to test the connection. When it says "Connected", you're done.

## Set up LM Studio

- Install LM Studio, download a model, and load it.

- Start LM Studio's local server.

- In Tidytalk, choose LM Studio at the top of Settings › Set Up AI, enter the name of the loaded model, save, and click the purple network icon to test the connection.

Local models don't need an API key, and Tidytalk gives them a 60-second timeout instead of 12 seconds.

## Choosing a model

- Tidying is a light task, but the model has to follow instructions: tidy what you said instead of answering it. Small models are less reliable at this and at following custom rules.

- A model around 7B parameters or larger is a good starting point. qwen2.5:7b is about a 5 GB download and handles both Chinese and English well.

- If the local model is slow or returns something unexpected, Tidytalk pastes the raw transcript, so you never lose what you said.

## No AI at all

Turn off "Tidy up text" in Settings › Set Up AI and Tidytalk becomes a fast, fully offline speech-to-text tool. Replacements, snippets, and Chinese–English spacing still work, because they run on your Mac without AI.

## Verify it yourself

Tidytalk is open source under the MIT License. You can read exactly what it sends and when on GitHub, or build it from source.

---

URL: https://tidytalk.zayen.dev/use-cases/developers/

# Talk to your AI coding tools instead of typing

Good prompts are long. Explaining a bug, a refactor, or a design decision out loud is faster than typing it, as long as the result reads like you wrote it.

{{updated}}

## Why speak your prompts

Most people speak much faster than they type, often two to three times as fast. With AI coding assistants, the quality of the answer depends on how much context you give, and context is exactly what gets cut when you're typing. Tidytalk lets you hold a shortcut, explain the problem the way you would to a colleague, and paste a clean, punctuated paragraph into Cursor, Claude, ChatGPT, your terminal, or a pull request.

## What it looks like

You say | Tidytalk pastes

Um, so the login test is flaky, it fails like one in ten times, I think it's because the, uh, the mock server isn't ready before the request, can you add a wait or, no, actually a retry with a timeout | The login test is flaky and fails about one in ten times. I think the mock server isn't ready before the request. Can you add a retry with a timeout?

We should probably, um, cache the user list because it's loaded like three times on the dashboard | We should probably cache the user list because it's loaded three times on the dashboard.

Your correction ("a wait or, no, actually a retry") keeps only the final version, and the fillers are gone. Nothing is summarized or added.

## Keep technical terms intact

Switch the mode to Code (keep terms) in Settings › Set Up AI › Tidying. Terms, commands, file names, and symbols are kept exactly as you said them, and punctuation isn't converted. If you speak Chinese, English terms you mix in, such as "API" or "rate limit", are kept exactly as you said them.

## Teach it your project's names

Speech recognition stumbles on names it has never heard: libraries, internal services, teammates. Two settings in Settings › Vocabulary fix this:

- Common words: list names like SenseVoice, Kubernetes, or your service names. The AI corrects similar-sounding mistakes to your spelling.

- Replacements: always turn a frequent mishearing into the right word, for example "cloud" into "Claude". These run on your Mac and work even with tidying off.

You can also add custom rules, such as "Write file names and commands in backticks", and Tidytalk follows them when it tidies.

## Rewrite a draft with your voice

Select a rough note, hold Right Option, and say "turn this into a commit message" or "make this a bulleted list for the PR description". The selection is replaced with the result, and if the rewrite fails your text isn't touched.

## Think in another language, write English

If English isn't your first language, set the output language to English and explain the problem in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, or Cantonese. Tidytalk tidies and translates in one step, which works well for English-only codebases and teams. See Dictate and translate.

## Keep code context private

Your voice is always recognized on your Mac. If your prompts mention proprietary code, point Tidytalk at a local model in Ollama or LM Studio so the text never leaves your machine either. See Private and offline dictation.

## Tips

- Double-tap the shortcut for hands-free recording when you want to talk through a long explanation.

- Use "Recent" in the menu bar to paste the last result again, for example into a second chat.

- Tidytalk works in any app with a text field, including VS Code, Cursor, Xcode, Terminal, Slack, and web apps.

---

URL: https://tidytalk.zayen.dev/use-cases/translation/

# Speak in your language, paste in theirs

Explain it the way you think, and send it in the language your reader needs. Tidytalk tidies and translates in one step.

{{updated}}

## How it works

- Choose an output language from the menu bar icon (Output Language), or in Settings › Set Up AI › Tidying.

- Hold Option + Command and speak in Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, or Cantonese. You don't need to pick the spoken language; it's detected automatically.

- Let go. Fillers and slips are removed, the text is translated, and the result is pasted at your cursor. The indicator shows a tag like "To English" while it works.

Output languages: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, and Spanish.

## Example

You say (Chinese) | Pasted (English)

嗯，那个，麻烦跟客户说一下我们下周三之前会把报价发过去，呃，有问题随时联系我 | Please let the client know we'll send the quote by next Wednesday. Feel free to contact me with any questions.

Exact wording depends on the AI model you use, but the meaning stays the same: Tidytalk translates what you said and doesn't add to it.

## Write formal email

Set the mode to Email (formal) to get complete, polite sentences in the target language, or Chat (casual) for quick messages. Your vocabulary still applies, so names and product terms come out spelled correctly.

## Switch languages quickly

- The Output Language submenu in the menu bar changes the language for your next dictation without opening Settings.

- Already pasted English but need it in Japanese too? Open "Recent" in the menu bar, choose the result, and pick "Re-tidy" with another language. It's pasted into the current text field without speaking again.

- To rewrite text you've already typed, select it, hold Right Option, and say "translate this into German".

## Good to know

- Translation and tidying happen in a single AI request, so it's about as fast as tidying alone.

- Questions and instructions are translated, not answered. "Can you check the logs?" comes out as a question in the target language.

- Translation needs "Tidy up text" turned on and an AI service. If the request fails, Tidytalk pastes the original text and tells you.

- For full privacy, use a local model. Larger local models translate noticeably better than small ones. See Private and offline dictation.

---

URL: https://tidytalk.zayen.dev/guides/mixed-chinese-english-dictation/

# How to dictate mixed Chinese and English on Mac

If you work in Chinese, your sentences are full of English: API, deadline, PR, product names. Here's how to set up Tidytalk so those words come out right, with proper spacing, without editing afterward.

{{updated}}

## What you get

You say | You get

嗯那个我想问一下就是这个 API 的那个 rate limit 呃是多少 | 我想问一下这个 API 的 rate limit 是多少？

项目要延期到下周三，不对，是下周四 | 项目要延期到下周四。

The English terms stay in English, fillers like 嗯、那个、就是说 are removed, the slip is corrected, and spaces are added between Chinese and English.

## 1. Pick a speech model that handles mixing

Open Settings › Speech Model. All models run on your Mac.

- SenseVoice (the default, about 240 MB) is fast and handles Mandarin with English mixed in well. Start here.

- Qwen3-ASR (about 1 GB) is the most accurate, and it uses your vocabulary while recognizing, so names and product terms come out right the first time. It's slower: about 4 seconds for 20 seconds of speech.

- Fun-ASR-Nano covers Chinese, English, and Japanese and is nearly as accurate as Qwen3-ASR.

- Avoid Whisper Turbo for Chinese, since it drops characters, and Apple Speech, which follows your system language and is weaker on mixed speech.

You don't choose a language before speaking. The language is detected automatically, sentence by sentence.

## 2. Add the English terms you use

Speech recognition gets rare names and jargon wrong more than anything else. In Settings › Vocabulary, list them under Common Words, one per line: your product names, colleagues' names, tools like Kubernetes or Figma.

- With Qwen3-ASR, these words are recognized correctly from the start.

- With any model, they're also given to the AI during tidying, so a similar-sounding mistake is corrected to your spelling.

- If one word is always wrong in the same way, add one under Replacements, for example "cloud" → "Claude". Replacements run on your Mac even with tidying off.

See how to teach dictation names and terms for more.

## 3. Let tidying keep your terms

Tidying removes fillers and slips and adds punctuation, but English words and technical terms inside Chinese speech are kept as they are. It never translates them into Chinese unless you ask it to.

- For technical writing, choose the Code (keep terms) mode in Settings › Set Up AI › Tidying. It keeps terms, commands, file names, and symbols exactly as you said them.

- For messages, the Chat (casual) mode keeps your tone and sentence-final particles.

## 4. Spacing is automatic

Tidytalk adds a space between Chinese and English or numbers, uses full-width punctuation after Chinese, and converts full-width letters and digits to half-width. Decimal points, file names, and URLs are left alone. It runs on your Mac and can be turned off in Settings › General.

## 5. Need it in English instead?

Set the output language to English, and you can speak Chinese and paste English. Translation happens in the same step as tidying, so it's about as fast. See Dictate and translate.

## Tips

- Say English terms the way you normally would. You don't need to slow down or spell them.

- If a result is wrong, open Recent in the menu bar, pick the result, and choose "Add to Vocabulary…" to fix the word for next time.

- If you fix a word yourself right after pasting, Tidytalk notices and offers to add it to your vocabulary. Nothing is added until you confirm.

---

URL: https://tidytalk.zayen.dev/guides/live-translated-captions/

# Live translated captions for any video or meeting on Mac

Watching a lecture in another language, or on a call where you miss half the words? Tidytalk captions whatever your Mac is playing and translates each sentence as it's spoken, in any app, with no browser extension.

{{updated}}

## What it can caption

Anything your Mac plays: YouTube or Bilibili in a browser, a downloaded video, a podcast, a course, or the other people on a Zoom, Teams, or Meet call. Tidytalk records only the computer's audio, never your microphone, so your own voice on a call isn't captioned.

## Set it up once

- Install Tidytalk and finish the setup guide.

- For translation, choose an AI service in Settings › Set Up AI. Ollama, LM Studio, or Apple Intelligence keep everything on your Mac; with a cloud service such as DeepSeek or OpenAI, caption text is sent to it.

- In Settings › Live Captions, turn on Translate Captions and pick a language under Translate To: English, Simplified or Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, or Spanish.

## Start captions

- Play the video or join the call.

- Press ⌃⌥C (Control + Option + C), or choose Start Listening under Live Captions in the menu bar menu. The first time, macOS asks you to allow Tidytalk to record system audio.

- The caption bar appears with one sentence per line and the translation underneath. While listening, the menu bar icon shows an orange dot.

- Press ⌃⌥C again to stop. The audio and text are cleared from memory.

## Translation as you listen

With Translate as You Listen on (the default), the sentence that's still being spoken is translated too and updates as it goes, so you're not waiting for the speaker to finish. When the sentence ends, the final translation replaces it. Turn it off in Settings › Live Captions to translate only finished sentences, which uses fewer AI calls. Sentences already in your target language are left alone.

## Caption just one app

By default Tidytalk captions all audio except its own sounds. To ignore notifications or music, pick a single app under Listen To in the menu bar menu or in Settings › Live Captions.

## Match the speech model to the video's language

- The default SenseVoice model recognizes Mandarin (with English mixed in), English, Japanese, Korean, and Cantonese.

- For other spoken languages, such as French or German, switch to Qwen3-ASR or Whisper Turbo in Settings › Speech Model.

## Make it look right

- Drag the caption bar anywhere; it remembers the spot.

- Choose a dark or glass style and a text size in Settings › Live Captions.

- It hides after 10 seconds of silence and comes back when there's sound. Hover over it for translate, pause, and close buttons.

## Paste what was just said

Taking notes? Put your cursor in a text field and press ⌃⌥V. Tidytalk tidies the latest passage, from the last pause of more than 2 seconds and up to 30 seconds, and pastes it. You can also hover over a sentence in the captions and click Paste to paste from there onward.

## Privacy

Audio is recognized on your Mac and never uploaded. With a local AI service or Apple Intelligence, the translation stays on your Mac too, and captions work fully offline. Nothing is saved after you stop listening.

URL: https://tidytalk.zayen.dev/guides/custom-vocabulary/

# How to make dictation get names and technical terms right

Speech recognition is good at everyday words and bad at the words that matter most to you: your colleagues' names, your product, your tools. Tidytalk gives you four ways to fix that, from the moment you speak to the text that's pasted.

{{updated}}

Everything here is in Settings › Vocabulary.

## 1. List your common words

Under Common Words, write the names, products, and terms you use, one per line. For example:
Kubernetes
Figma
Claude
SenseVoice

These words help at two stages:

- While recognizing: with Qwen3-ASR as the speech model (Settings › Speech Model), these words are recognized correctly from the start. This works even with tidying off.

- While tidying: with any model, the list is given to the AI, so a similar-sounding mistake is corrected to your spelling. This needs "Tidy up text" on.

## 2. Add replacements for repeat mistakes

If a word is always misheard the same way, add a replacement, for example "cloud" → "Claude". English matching ignores case and only matches whole words, so "cloudy" is left alone. Replacements run on your Mac and work even with tidying off.

The quickest way to add one: open Recent in the menu bar, pick the result that went wrong, and choose "Add to Vocabulary…".

## 3. Let it learn from your corrections

When you fix a word yourself right after pasting, in the same text field, Tidytalk notices. The change is listed under Edits Found in the menu bar and at the top of Settings › Vocabulary. Nothing is added until you click "Add to Vocabulary".

It only compares within about a minute and a half of pasting and saves nothing. You can turn it off at the bottom of the Vocabulary page.

## 4. Write rules for how things are written

Custom Rules control style rather than spelling, one per line, up to 20. For example:

- Write amounts as digits.

- Write the product name as Tidytalk.

- Write times in 24-hour format.

Tidying and voice rewrite follow them. Rules only change how things are written; they never make the AI add content.

## Bonus: snippets

Say only a short phrase such as "my email" to paste a full email address, an address, or a canned reply. A snippet is used only when the whole recording is that phrase, never when it comes up mid-sentence.

## Which one should I use?

Problem | Fix

A name or term is misspelled in different ways | Common Words, ideally with Qwen3-ASR

The same wrong word appears every time | Replacements

You keep fixing words after pasting | Let Edits Found suggest them

Spelling is right, but the style isn't | Custom Rules

You type the same long text again and again | Snippets

Speak Chinese with English terms? See how to dictate mixed Chinese and English.
